summary: Sound stage-1 rewrite. It reuses a kernel that is proven correct (s5, 71e40388: 19/19 bisect, coherent data, two-state replays) in a regime where its known weakness, the serial per-tile chain, matters least: about 2 tiles per CTA at sliding verify_16. A hard per-band gate and PATH CHOSEN lines make a single check readable without companions. The real risks are the unmeasured low-occupancy latency plus the ticket-merge tail, and the run's wall clock.
justification: Mechanism. In the board profile, sliding verify_16 is 22.6 us: FA3 main 10.7, combine 3.8, pre-attn 2.7, plus prepare and rms_norm_gate outside the top 3. Sliding verify_32 is 29.0 us: FA3 14.8, combine 4.3, pre-attn 4.1. The floors are 1.9 and 3.7 us, so roughly 18 and 22.6 us of replaced launches sit 5-10x above the floor. That makes the target launch count and dependent round trips, not bandwidth. A full window is 2055 keys, which is 33 tiles of 64 per request. 16 x 33 = 528 tiles at grid 264 is about 2 tiles per CTA, so most of s5's measured 3.8 us/tile is chain latency, not repeated serially. The expected directions match TASK.md: weight 46 per sliding verify row, verify_16/32 faster, verify_1 flat unless gated in, full/decode untouched. The milestones are readable from top_kernels, since the new kernel replaces four named kernels with one. Prior. The frontmatter has no `prior:` field, but the body names every relevant ancestor: held full-verify-wgmma-s4-sliding-window (same idea, built on the broken s3 branch), sliding-verify-cuda-streamk-window and sliding-verify-sk-pseudo-decode-s1 (mma.sync, 0.653x/0.482x at B=16/32). The FINDINGS/DIAGNOSIS do-not-try entry is 'mma.sync for q_len-8 verify at B>=16', and DIAGNOSIS says 'the wgmma line replaces this approach'. The difference (FP8 wgmma tensor-core path vs mma.sync) is real, and this is DIAGNOSIS action 2. So it is not a duplicate. WEAKEST LINK: s5 has never been timed at low occupancy, and the ticket merge is a serial tail. The only s5 timing is full verify at B=16/32 (288.7/429.5 us, ~76 tiles per CTA), where latency overlapped across many tiles. Here every CTA's first tile has a fully exposed cold-L2 gather plus S, transpose, softmax and PV, then a partial write and an atomic. The last-arriving CTA per request then merges about 16-17 fp32 partials (8 tokens x 16 heads x 64 plus m/l, about 33 KB each, about 0.55 MB per request) and runs norm-gate from one SM. Merge plus norm-gate alone could cost several us, so the M2 target (<= 12 us replaced) is plausible but not assured. Fan-in vs per-CTA tile count is exactly what the {2B, 4B, 8B, SM, 2xSM} per-grid table resolves, so the design can find the right point. At verify_1 (33 tiles), any grid either fans in 33 partials to one CTA or serialises 4-8 tiles per CTA, against a 9.9 us PSEUDO incumbent. Flat via the gate is the realistic outcome there.
confounders: restack-sk-pseudo-cluster-plus-v3-fused-preattn: owns the sliding verify_1 incumbent (PSEUDO sk route). The B=1 gate compares against it, not against FA3. A verify_1 move is attributable only via PATH CHOSEN; if the band stays on master, verify_1 is a re-measure.

fused-preattention-triton: the new path keeps _pre_attention_kernel unchanged (ROPE on, PAIRED=False), the same node master runs before FA3. Its 2.7/4.1 us is common to both sides and is not a confounder, as long as the builder does not touch it.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing / paired-heads-launch-cleanup: their predicate is window == 0, so sliding verify is unpaired on master and on this branch. No interaction, but the route predicate must stay disjoint from `paired` and `pseudo` (checked before or instead of _ps_gate) so B=1 does not take two routes.

All four existing load_inline modules (splitkv, sk/PSEUDO, skF, slide): no numerical interaction. They share the run's wall clock, though. DIAGNOSIS puts import at 222 s across 4 modules, s5's module compiled in 33.9 s, and s5's whole check took ~430 s. A fifth module plus a 3-band x 5-grid x 31-median gate and the full self-check suite can approach the 15-minute run limit, and a timeout is charged.
interference: No companions. This is kind: rewrite, judged on the replaced kernels' own time per shape. The per-band hard gate prints every grid's time against the band's master incumbent, measured in the same process with cold-L2 graph replay. PATH CHOSEN lines say which path ran on each scored row. Together these make a gain, a loss and 'gated off' all unambiguous from the one log plus top_kernels. An ab-revert of any landed hypothesis would not change what this run measures, because the replaced FA3/combine/norm-gate chain has had no landed tuning on sliding verify. A control isolating a sub-change (window mask vs the s5 kernel) is meaningless: s5 at window=0 is already measured (0.570x/0.704x on full). One forward-looking caveat: queued sliding-verify-fa3-num-splits-band-gate changes this hypothesis's incumbent on the same rows. If both run on the same day, do not stack them blind. Whichever lands second must re-gate against the new master, and this run's gate numbers are valid only against the master it was built on.
rules_flags: Run wall clock: a fifth load_inline module (~34 s) on top of ~222 s of imports, plus self-checks and the per-grid gate, risks the 15-minute run limit, which is charged as a timeout. Budget the gate (e.g. median of 31 only for the grid finalists, a quick pass of ~7 to prune grids) and print elapsed time per phase.

Tail-tile page-index prefetch: tiles start at lo_b, not 64-aligned, so the last tile is usually partial (2055 = 32*64 + 7 keys). The page_table reads for keys >= seq_b must be predicated or clamped. A masked logit does not stop an out-of-bounds or garbage page index from being dereferenced in the cp.async gather.
Route-table selection by timing at import/prepare on synthetic inputs is fine (master's _sd_gate precedent). It must freeze a config-only table and must never re-time or branch on data in kernel_fn.

Ticket arrays must be self-resetting per launch and sized by config; no module-global pointer into a state's tensors (two-state rotation, moe g_maps lesson). Already specified, and s5 passed this. Keep it verbatim.
Every key: the windowed mask t >= seq_b - 8 + j - (window - 1) matches FA3 window_size=(window - 1, 0) and the task's last-2048-token window. No block skipping inside [lo_b, seq_b). OK as specified.
open_questions: The self-check uses kv_scale 1 and 0.25, but the judge's own sliding page-1 verify test uses kv_scale 0.015625 (batch 3, ctx 4000). Add 1/64 to the self-check, or exclude kv_scale != 1 from the route config-only, so the first failing case is not a judge test.

Per the new single-round selector lesson (1.02x selectors mis-routed bf16 today): the 1.05x threshold has margin, but a second interleaved gate round with an IQR bound for each band that would route is cheap insurance against a noisy route at verify_16/32.

Print, per grid, kernel-only time and the ticket-merge tail separately (e.g. a no-merge DBG variant, or a clock64 stamp on the last CTA). If M2 is missed, stage 2 then knows whether to attack first-tile latency (PDL from pre-attention, prefetch) or merge fan-in (two-level or cluster DSMEM merge).
Retire or mark superseded the held full-verify-wgmma-s4-sliding-window and sliding-verify-cuda-streamk-window queue items, so a later tick does not run the same idea again on the broken base.

Does the gate's B=2..16 band (timed only at B=16) risk routing small-B tests (B=3/4/5 ragged, ctx 4000-6000) through a grid tuned for 528 tiles? Correctness is covered by the self-check; only speed at unscored B is affected, which is acceptable but worth noting.
